title: A Unifying Framework for Concept-Based Representational Similarity
abstract: arXiv:2606.09653v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Learned representations across models and modalities often exhibit striking structural similarities, suggesting shared underlying concept decompositions. However, concept alignment remains poorly defined: existing approaches optimize different objectives under the same terminology, obscuring what is actually aligned. We propose a unifying framework that decomposes alignment along two axes: what is aligned (representations vs. concepts) and at what level (instance-wise vs. distributional). This induces four corresponding properties---instance-wise and distributional variants of translation and concept consistency---and reveals precisely which of these guarantees existing methods provide. We further introduce InterVenchA, an intervention-based benchmark that separately measures extraction quality, translation quality, and concept consistency---which we validate against human perception of concept alignment. translated_title: 基于概念的表征相似性统一框架
translated_abstract: 跨模型与跨模态学习到的表征往往呈现出惊人的结构相似性，这暗示它们共享潜在的concept分解。然而，concept对齐的定义仍然模糊不清：现有方法在相同术语下优化着不同的目标，掩盖了实际被对齐的内容。我们提出了一个统一框架，沿两个轴对对齐进行分解：对齐的对象（表征 vs. concept）以及对齐的层级（实例级 vs. 分布级）。由此引出四种相应的性质——translation和concept一致性的实例级与分布级变体——并精确揭示了现有方法提供了其中哪些保证。我们进一步介绍了InterVenchA，这是一个基于干预的基准，分别测量提取质量、translation质量和concept一致性——我们依据人类对concept对齐的感知对该基准进行了验证。利用该框架，我们……
tldr: 提出了一个基于概念的表征相似性统一框架，沿“对齐对象”与“对齐层级”两个轴分解concept对齐问题，并引入基于干预的基准InterVenchA，分别测量提取质量、translation质量与concept一致性，且与人类感知进行对照验证。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes a unifying framework for concept-based representational similarity that decomposes alignment along two axes—what is aligned (representations vs. concepts) and at what level (instance-wise vs. distributional)—and introduces InterVenchA, an intervention-based benchmark that separately measures extraction quality, translation quality, and concept consistency, validated against human perception.
